You are implementing Task 11 of the `inter.face` build: the two worker agent specs. inter.face is a cross-agent design plugin made of markdown; an agent reads it and follows it, there is no runtime.

Working directory: `/Users/taha/Documents/inter.face` (git branch `build/plugin-files`).

**Read this first — your requirements:**
`.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-01-inter-face-build/task-11-brief.md`

**Read what dispatches you:** `loops/01-direction.md` (§8/§9 dispatch `surface-designer`), `loops/02-craft.md` (dispatches `technique-prototyper`). **Read what you must obey:** `PRINCIPLES.md`, `SURFACES.md`, `CRAFT.md`, `STYLES.md`.
**Mine for craft rules:** `docs/audit/competitor-imagegen.md`.

Create `agents/surface-designer.md` and `agents/technique-prototyper.md`, each with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) matching the pattern in `/Users/taha/Documents/portfolio.me/agents/section-designer.md`.

---

## `agents/surface-designer.md`

One agent per surface **per concept**, one image each, never a compressed board — *a compressed board hides exactly the detail the human needs to judge.*

**CARRIED CONSTRAINT — you must close a gap the loops depend on.** `loops/01-direction.md` §10 runs a set-level anti-repeat check that rejects a set when *"the same composition anchor repeats more than twice running"* or *"the same background mode three times"*. **Neither term is defined anywhere in this repo.** With free-form labels chosen independently by parallel workers, that check is unfalsifiable and passes vacuously.

So: **define both vocabularies here, as closed menus**, and require each worker to log one pick from each. `docs/audit/competitor-imagegen.md` (search for "composition anchor" and "background mode") has the source menus — use them, adapt to cover tool-shaped surfaces too. A closed menu is what makes the loop's check able to fail. This is the single most important thing in this task.

**Also required:**
- **Platform mode** honored (iOS / Android / cross-platform-neutral) per `SURFACES.md`.
- **Safe-area bands** — every mobile surface image shows or reserves four bands: status, title/nav, content, bottom-nav/home-indicator. *A screen running edge-to-edge in all four directions has failed regardless of how it looks.*
- **Aspect ratio** taken from `loops/01-direction.md`'s per-class table — do not restate a different number.
- **Text-in-image constraints** per `PRINCIPLES.md` `§9`: realistic copy lengths, minimal text per image, no invented brand names, no placeholder superlatives.
- **Device framing inverted from the source skill's default:** bare screen unless physicality is load-bearing. A phone bezel eats ~30% of the canvas and pulls the model's fidelity toward rendering a handset instead of the interface under review.
- **Embarrassment self-gate** before returning: would a designer put their name on this? Reject in the worker — cheaper than at Gate A.
- The **return contract**: the image, plus the logged composition anchor and background mode.

## `agents/technique-prototyper.md`

One agent per technique. Delivers a standalone runnable HTML file, a screenshot, a **measured** frame rate under load, the byte cost, all required states for the surface class (three render states page-shaped; the nine data states are `TOOLS.md`'s and belong to the build, not the prototype), and a verdict — **ship / cut / ship-with-caveat** — carrying a **TESTED / PARTIAL / INFERRED** evidence label per `loops/02-craft.md`.

Free rein while prototyping (any library, any CDN); that freedom ends at handoff where `§7` requires everything vendored.

**Report failure honestly — failing cheap here is the entire point of the loop.** A rejected prototype is never argued into acceptance, tuned during the build, or carried forward on the theory that it comes together in integration.

---

**Conventions:** both files must address **page-shaped** and **tool-shaped**. Backticked `` `§N` `` = a `PRINCIPLES.md` rule; own-section refs take above/below, never bare `(§N)`. Markdown links to files that exist are fine; `AGENTS.md`, `skills/`, `commands/` do not exist yet — backticks only. State that an agent which cannot spawn subagents reads the file and does the work inline. No placeholders.

**Steps:** read → write both → run `./scripts/check.sh` (no new failures, no placeholder hits, links resolve) → commit both with the brief's message.

**Report contract:** full report to `.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-01-inter-face-build/task-11-report.md` — what you shipped, **the two closed menus you defined and where each term came from**, and the check output.

Return ONLY: status, commit SHA, one-line check summary, concerns.

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best
code is the code never written.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.
3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
4. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

**Bug fix = root cause, not symptom.** A report names a symptom. Before you
edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications with a `ponytail:` comment (`// ponytail: this exists`), simple reads as intent, not ignorance. Shortcut with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic)? The comment names the ceiling and the upgrade path: `# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`.

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Never lazy about understanding the problem. The ladder shortens the
solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.
"}}

1	# Loop 1 — Direction
2	
3	**Goal:** decide what this surface is, who it is for, what it must not become, and what it
4	looks like — and get a human to agree before anything expensive exists.
5	
6	**Input:** [`TRANSLATE.md`](../TRANSLATE.md), all six rows filled. Row 1 blank means this
7	loop cannot start; it does not start generic.
8	
9	**Output:** the direction half of `DIRECTION.md`, one rendered image per surface per
10	concept, and a signed Gate A.
11	
12	```text
13	0 branch        1 class        2 platform      3 access        4 derive
14	redesign or     page-shaped    iOS / Android   the Loop 1      physical experience
15	greenfield      tool-shaped    or neutral      decision list   → three directions
16	                                                                     │
17	5 palette ─► 6 type ─► 7 concepts ─► 8 ratio ─► 9 dispatch ─► 10 set check ─► Gate A
18	per          per        one per       per class  one agent per  per concept,    human
19	direction,   direction  direction,    announce   surface per    anti-repeat     decides
20	sampled once            both tests    N first    concept
21	```
22	
23	---
24	
25	## The fork
26	
27	Read row 1 of `TRANSLATE.md` before anything else in this file, because it changes what
28	every step below is looking for.
29	
30	**Page-shaped** — read for seconds, once. The concepts compete on the opening move: what a
31	viewer understands in three seconds without reading a word. The surface list is a scroll
32	order. The images are horizontal, the aspect ratios in §8 below say which.
33	
34	**Tool-shaped** — read for hours, daily, by the same person. The concepts compete on the
35	operator's day: which of the forty-times-a-day actions gets the layout. The surface list is
36	a screen inventory keyed to tasks, not a scroll. `§15` binds **[HARD]** here, which means
37	the keyboard map is a Loop 1 artifact and not a Loop 4 discovery, and `STYLES.md`'s
38	style-under-density line is a gating question rather than a note.
39	
40	Both classes run every step below. They answer them differently, and the places where the
41	answer forks are marked.
42	
43	---
44	
45	## 0. Branch: is this a redesign?
46	
47	A surface that already exists is not a blank page, and running this loop as if it were is
48	how a working position gets replaced by a template with better spacing.
49	
50	Read [`REDESIGN.md`](../REDESIGN.md) and classify the ask before anything else. It is a
51	fork, not a slider — there is no "mostly a correction."
52	
53	| Classification | What this loop does |
54	|---|---|
55	| **Greenfield** | Start at §1 below. Nothing to preserve, so nothing to ask |
56	| **Correction** — the position is right, execution drifted | **This loop does not run.** `REDESIGN.md`'s fix ladder runs against the extracted system, with its per-fix discipline as the stop. Any fix that touches position leaves the pass and escalates to Gate A |
57	| **Reposition** — the position itself is wrong | This loop runs **in full**, with `CURRENT.md` as an input constraint rather than a blank page, and with the survival list written *before* §1 below rather than during it |
58	| **Conformance** — `TRANSLATE.md` row 6 names a design system the surface must obey | Neither path. `TRANSLATE.md`'s escape hatch fires, `PRINCIPLES.md`'s `§1`–`§3` are suspended wholesale
59	(that file's rules, not this file's steps), and `BREAKING.md`'s recording rule covers writing that down. Route to conformance and say so plainly |
60	
61	**On the reposition path, two things enter this loop that a greenfield run never carries.**
62	`CURRENT.md` — the extracted rendered system, measured and not yet adjudicated — is an input
63	to §4 below, because a derived direction that ignores what is already on the screen is a
64	greenfield direction wearing a redesign's name. And the **survival list**: what is
65	load-bearing, in `REDESIGN.md`'s sense of what breaks *outside* this surface if it changes.
66	Every concept in §7 below is built against that list, and a concept that quietly drops an
67	item on it has not been proposed, it has been mis-scoped.
68	
69	**The classification is falsifiable and the gates check it.** Three Gate A rejections on a
70	correction path means the ask was a reposition all along. The escalation runs one way only.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## 1. Set the surface class
75	
76	`TRANSLATE.md` row 1: `page-shaped` or `tool-shaped`, set once **per surface**, not once per
77	product. A product with a marketing site and an application behind login is two runs sharing
78	a palette and a type system, not one run averaging them — and the averaged run is the one
79	that ships a dashboard with a landing page's spacing scale.
80	
81	Write it in `DIRECTION.md` now. Every file this loop reads forks on it first.
82	
83	## 2. Set platform mode, if this runs on a phone or a tablet
84	
85	[`SURFACES.md`](../SURFACES.md) §1 — **iOS-native**, **Android-native**, or
86	**cross-platform-neutral**. One branch, chosen before a style and before a target number,
87	written into `DIRECTION.md` before Gate A.
88	
89	They do not mix. A neutral surface that borrows Liquid Glass for its content cards has
90	broken Apple's rule and its own in one move. A platform-committed surface that adopts the
91	other platform's numbers is wrong on both. `SURFACES.md` carries every number; none of them
92	are opinions and none of them get rounded.
93	
94	Web-only, desktop-only surfaces skip this step and record that they skipped it.
95	
96	## 3. Run the `ACCESS.md` Loop 1 decisions
97	
98	[`ACCESS.md`](../ACCESS.md) §13 is a list of thirteen decisions both classes owe, six more
99	tool-shaped, and four more native. **They run here, before a single image generates**, and
100	they land in `DIRECTION.md` as answers.
101	
102	This is not an audit moved earlier. These are shapes, not defects: a non-drag affordance
103	occupies layout space, a grid and a table are two different keyboard experiences of the same
104	visual, a focus ring has to be drawn against every background it can land on. None of them
105	are fixable in Loop 8 — you redraw.
106	
107	Three of them constrain the next two steps directly and are worth doing in order: whether
108	the sampled accent can carry body text, a 3:1 graphical role, or neither (which constrains
109	§5 below); the contrast boundary, stated rather than assumed; and the target-size route,
110	whose spacing unit enters the scale before the type scale does.
111	
112	`§10` is **[HARD]**. A row the human chooses not to answer is recorded as a decision with
113	its cost per `§16`, never as silence.
114	
115	## 4. Derive the direction — do not pick one
116	
117	Invoke [`STYLES.md`](../STYLES.md)'s **"Before the list: derive, don't pick"** procedure,
118	then its five-input **"Picking one"** procedure. In that order. The first generates, the
119	second cuts, and running them backwards produces a shortlist that started in a catalog.
120	
121	The short version, because the failure it prevents is the most common one in this pipeline:
122	read the archetype words from `TRANSLATE.md` row 4, ask what physical, spatial, or material
123	experience would embody them if design were not involved, and derive three visual directions
124	from *that*. Each stated in one concrete sentence naming a real-world referent. **If your
125	sentence contains only adjectives, it is not concrete enough**, and if you find yourself
126	reaching for a Swiss grid or a terminal by reflex you are reading your training data rather
127	than the subject.
128	
129	Then read the families — to name what you derived, to learn what it implies technically, and
130	to be warned how it fails. Not to generate it.
131	
132	**What this step hands to the next one, stated because the singular is a trap.**
133	`STYLES.md` ends its procedure with *"never one answer — bring three directions to Gate A."*
134	That is binding, and it means **the directions do not collapse here.** Two or three survive
135	the cut, and **each surviving direction becomes one concept in §7 below.** Directions and
136	concepts are the same objects at two stages of development, not two rounds of generation.
137	
138	So §5 and §6 below run **once per surviving direction**, not once for the run — a letterpress
139	direction and a cockpit direction do not share a neutral ramp or a typeface, and a palette
140	built before the directions exist is a palette built for none of them. The one thing genuinely
141	shared is the sampled accent, because the subject has one logo (§5 below).
142	
143	Two further outputs of this step are gating and both are easy to skip:
144	
145	- **The collision or subversion**, per `STYLES.md`, per direction. One parent carries
146	  structure, the other carries surface, and which is which gets named now rather than during
147	  the build.
148	- **The style-under-density line**, in the form *at forty rows this does X*. Asked at Gate A
149	  because the answer is sometimes *it cannot* — and a direction that is beautiful, coherent,
150	  correct for the archetype and structurally incapable of the surface it was chosen for is a
151	  finding worth having before the images are signed off. Tool-shaped surfaces cannot proceed
152	  without this line. Page-shaped surfaces owe it wherever real data lands.
153	
154	## 5. Palette — sampled from reality, in OKLCH, as pairs
155	
156	**Sampled once. Built out per direction.** `§6`: pull the accent from the subject or product's
157	real logo, product, or work. Sample the pixels. There is one subject and one logo, so there is
158	one sample, and every direction from §4 above reconciles against it. No existing brand means a
159	deliberate choice defended by one sentence of physical scene, then reconciled against
160	`TRANSLATE.md` row 3.
161	
162	Then build out **once per direction**: an accent, a substrate, a neutral ramp, and the full
163	state set — and tool-shaped, the status vocabulary from `TOOLS.md`, which needs shape or label
164	as well as color because `§10` forbids color alone. The same sampled hex sits at a different
165	chroma, against a different substrate, in a different ramp in each of the two or three
166	directions; that divergence is a large part of what Gate A is choosing between.
167	
168	Work in **OKLCH**, and write gradient endpoints in `oklch()`, because a single hex or `rgb()`
169	endpoint silently drops the whole interpolation back to muddy sRGB.
170	
171	**Every color ships as a pair** — the swatch and the foreground that is legal on it, with its
172	measured ratio at the size it is actually used (`STYLES.md`, paired color tokens). A swatch
173	with no foreground is an unfinished token and does not enter `DIRECTION.md`. Pairs extend to
174	every state and to the focus ring, and they are paired **per mode**: a foreground legal on
175	the light swatch tells you nothing about the dark one.
176	
177	Declare now whether the two modes are one design in two palettes or **two art directions**.
178	If the derived direction is atmospheric, motion-native, or material-heavy, the answer is two
179	art directions and both get built.
180	
181	## 6. Type
182	
183	**Per direction, like §5 above.** Two families at most, one if the direction earns it. Variable where the design drives an
184	axis, self-hosted and subset per `§7`, and checked against the actual script per `§13` — a
185	Persian, Arabic, or Devanagari subject needs a face that draws it, not one that falls back.
186	
187	**Every font decision carries its reason on the same line**: what this face does for this
188	direction that the obvious one would not. `STYLES.md`'s ban is on convergence, not on the
189	typeface — a bare blacklist goes stale in eighteen months and a reason survives.
190	
191	Tool-shaped surfaces add one requirement here: tabular figures on every column of numbers
192	that updates. It is one declaration and it is not optional.
193	
194	## 7. Develop each direction into a concept
195	
196	One concept per surviving direction from §4 above, carrying that direction's palette and type
197	from §5 and §6. This is development, not a fresh generation — a concept invented here, with no
198	direction behind it, has skipped the derivation and will read like it.
199	
200	The conductor does this, not a worker. `§1`–`§4` are asking for the collision, the opening
201	move, and the thing nobody expects, and that is exactly where a cheaper model reaches for
202	the category reflex these rules exist to prevent.
203	
204	Each concept states:
205	
206	- **The collision or subversion**, as one sentence, with the structural parent named
207	- **The opening move** — page-shaped, what happens in the first three seconds; tool-shaped,
208	  what the operator sees when they open this at 9am with forty things waiting
209	- **How the primary content is presented** — invent it. Not a card grid by reflex: a flexible
210	  card layout puts each item's attributes in a different place from the last, so a reader
211	  comparing them scans back and forth hunting for what moved. A list, a table, or a filmstrip
212	  holds position from item to item and is the more honest default whenever the things
213	  genuinely are comparable
214	- **How navigation works**, and tool-shaped, the keyboard path through the primary workflow
215	- **What happens when something is missing or wrong** — page-shaped, the 404 and the failed
216	  submission, in this concept rather than the framework's default. Tool-shaped, `TOOLS.md`'s
217	  nine data states, with empty, permission denied, and conflict named specifically: the first
218	  is what every new user sees, the last is the one that destroys work
219	- **The surface list and its order**, derived from row 2's viewer and their task
220	
221	### The two distinctness tests
222	
223	`§4` says bring 2–3 distinct concepts. As a bare instruction that is what six of seven
224	audited skills already fail at, two of them by asking the model to simulate a random number
225	generator — which returns its prior with extra steps. So distinctness is tested **on the
226	artifact**, not asserted about the process. Both tests run before anything reaches Gate A.
227	
228	> **Swap test.** If someone could swap the headline text between two concepts without
229	> noticing, they are too similar.
230	>
231	> **Tool-shaped surfaces frequently have no headline**, so swap what they do have: the screen
232	> title, the primary action's label, and the empty state's copy. If all three move between two
233	> concepts unnoticed, the concepts differ in styling and not in how the operator's day is
234	> organized — which is the only axis this class is choosing on.
235	
236	> **Family pass.** Label each concept with a concrete noun of your own choosing — *exhibition,
237	> cockpit, playbill, field-manual*. If two share a label, or a label applies equally well to
238	> another concept, rework. Do not use a fixed vocabulary for the labels; a fixed vocabulary is
239	> the catalog problem again, one level up.
240	
241	Then the **category-reflex check**, from `STYLES.md`'s cliché fence: if a concept is guessable
242	from "surface for a \<category\>" alone, or from category-plus-obvious-twist, throw it out.
243	Note one concept you rejected and why, so the human sees the range rather than the survivors.
244	
245	## 8. Aspect ratio, keyed to the surface class
246	
247	**This is where a real bug lived.** "One horizontal image per surface" was inherited from a
248	parent whose surfaces were all web page sections. A phone screen is roughly 9:19.5; rendering
249	it on a 16:9 canvas spends about three quarters of the model's fidelity budget on empty
250	background. State the ratio per class:
251	
252	| Surface | Canvas | What is in it |
253	|---|---|---|
254	| Page-shaped web section | 16:9, hero 21:9 | One section |
255	| Tool-shaped desktop screen | 16:10 | One screen, full chrome, real row counts |
256	| Phone screen | 4:5 for one screen, or 16:9 holding 2–3 phone-portrait screens at identical scale | One step of the flow |
257	| Tablet screen | 4:3 or 16:10 | One screen, at a stated width |
258	
259	Two to three phones on one canvas is the **only** exception to never compressing a board,
260	and it holds because they are the same surface across a flow at readable scale rather than
261	different surfaces stacked. The moment type stops being legible, drop to one phone per canvas.
262	
263	**Announce N before generating.** **N is the surface count, not the image count** — and every
264	concept is rendered across all N, so three concepts and nine surfaces is twenty-seven images.
265	Write both numbers in text before generating — *"three concepts, nine surfaces, twenty-seven
266	images"* — and label every image **"\<concept label>: Surface X of N — \<name\>"**, with the
267	label from the family pass in §7 above, so the three renders of the same surface never collide.
268	
269	That 3× is the real cost of `§4` and it is paid deliberately. **If it is not affordable, cut to
270	two concepts rather than to a partial set** — a concept rendered at three surfaces cannot be
271	compared against one rendered at nine, and the set-level check in §10 below has nothing to run
272	on. Two complete concepts is a choice. Three partial ones is a preference dressed as one.
273	
274	Committing to the numbers first makes stopping early a visible contradiction rather than a
275	silent one, and silent under-generation is the failure this costs one line to prevent.
276	
277	## 9. Dispatch `surface-designer`
278	
279	**One agent per surface per concept, one image each.** Never compress multiple surfaces into
280	one board, and never compress two concepts into one either: a
281	compressed board hides exactly the detail the human needs to judge, and what it hides first is
282	the smallest type and the primary action.
283	
284	Each agent receives the concept, the palette with its pairs, the type system, the collision
285	sentence, the platform mode, and the aspect ratio for its class. Each returns its image, its
286	logged composition anchor, and its logged background mode — the log exists so §10 below has
287	something to compare, since no single worker can see its neighbors.
288	
289	A second **detail image** of the same surface is permitted on demand, focused on typography
290	and spacing at larger scale, when the human at Gate A cannot read something. It is not a
291	redesign and not a variant: same design system, cleaner render.
292	
293	## 10. The set-level check
294	
295	Run by the conductor, on what comes back, **once per concept** — the set is one concept's N
296	surfaces, since that is the set a human reads as one thing. No worker can run it.
297	
298	Reject the set and regenerate the offending surfaces if:
299	
300	- the same **composition anchor** repeats more than **twice in a row**
301	- the same **background mode** repeats more than **three times in a row**
302	- **no full-bleed treatment appears anywhere** in the set
303	
304	**Suspended for a deliberately minimal brief** — typography-only, ultra-reductive, restraint
305	as the stated direction. There, sameness is the design and this check would be arguing with
306	the brief. Say out loud that it was suspended and why, so a later reader does not read a
307	uniform set as an oversight.
308	
309	Also check what the set does *not* vary: **within one concept**, palette, type hierarchy,
310	component family, and surface treatment stay identical across every image. Composition,
311	emphasis, and visual tempo are where variation belongs. A set that varies the palette has not
312	produced range, it has produced three different products. Across concepts the opposite holds —
313	palette and type *must* differ, because that is what §5 and §6 above built per direction and
314	what Gate A is choosing between.
315	
316	---
317	
318	> ## Gate A — human decision. `§16` **[HARD]**
319	>
320	> **Presented:**
321	>
322	> - **The rendered images**, per concept, all N surfaces of each, labeled
323	> - **The palette per concept**, as pairs, each with its measured ratio, and the one sampled
324	>   source they all reconcile against
325	> - **The type system per concept**, each family with its reason on the same line
326	> - **The collision sentence** per concept, with the structural parent named
327	> - **The style-under-density line** — *at forty rows this does X*
328	> - **The `ACCESS.md` answers**, and any row deferred, with its cost
329	> - **A SAFE / RISK split**, below. Not optional and not one risk
330	>
331	> **The SAFE / RISK split.** Coherence is table stakes; this is the part that separates one
332	> run from another. Present the safe reading of the direction, then **at least two risks**,
333	> each with **what it costs** if it lands badly — in bytes, in build time, in the audience it
334	> loses, in the thing it makes harder later. A risk with no stated cost is a pitch. Two risks
335	> is the floor because one risk is a recommendation wearing a choice's clothes.
336	>
337	> **The anti-shortcut clause.** This gate is not a status update and `DIRECTION.md` is not a
338	> substitute for it: **the written output is the OUTPUT of the interactive review**. If there
339	> is any non-trivial finding, the path to proceeding goes through the human. A gate that
340	> becomes a paragraph somebody reads later has been removed, not satisfied.
341	>
342	> **They may pick a concept, pick pieces across concepts, or send it back.** Iterating here
343	> is far cheaper than iterating in code, and this is the last point where the direction is
344	> free to move.
345	>
346	> **Deferrals get priced, in a table:**
347	>
348	> | decision needed | if deferred, what happens |
349	> |---|---|
350	> | Reduced-motion still frame not art-directed | Ships as `animation: none` — a plain freeze where a composed frame was |
351	> | Second and third concept not generated | The direction has nothing to be chosen against; the first idea wins by default, which is `§1`'s failure mode |
352	> | Style-under-density line not written | A family that cannot hold forty rows is discovered at build, with the images already approved |
353	> | `ACCESS.md` grid-or-table row left open | The keyboard model gets decided by whoever writes the component, in Loop 4, from the visual |
354	> | Platform mode left unset on a native surface | Every number below it forks, and discovering the fork during the build is a rewrite |
355	>
356	> State the cost once, accept the answer, carry it into the run's confidence, and do not
357	> raise it again.
358	
359	---
360	
361	## When Gate A rejects
362	
363	**Diagnose before regenerating anything.** The three rejections go to three different places
364	and treating them alike is how a run burns its budget re-rendering a correct image.
365	
366	| What was rejected | Where it goes back to |
367	|---|---|
368	| **Execution** — wrong palette in the render, wrong crop, the image did not capture the concept | Regenerate those images with corrected direction. Same concept, same surface list, same collision |
369	| **Concept** — the collision does not land, the opening move is wrong, the content is presented wrong | Back to §7 above. New concepts, not a patch on the rejected one |
370	| **Brief** — their reaction reveals the surface class, the viewer, the archetype, or the anti-positioning was misread | Back to `TRANSLATE.md`. Fix the table first. Designing on a misread table produces another rejection at the same gate |
371	
372	The third row is the one that gets missed. **When the human says the images look fine and
373	still sounds unhappy, the table is the suspect, not the render.**
374	
375	**Three rejections at the same gate means the translation table is wrong, not the work.**
376	Stop iterating. Re-open `TRANSLATE.md`, fix the row that is wrong, and come back through this
377	gate. The fourth attempt at the same gate has never worked. On a redesign, that same count
378	carries the second diagnosis from §0 above: three Gate A rejections on a correction path
379	means the ask was a reposition from the start.
380	
381	**Record what the rejection revealed**, not only the correction. What they reacted against,
382	and what that says about the viewer, the archetype, or the risk appetite the table failed to
383	capture. Recording only the correction throws away the more valuable half of it.
384	
385	## Skip costs
386	
387	| Skipping | Costs |
388	|---|---|
389	| §3, the `ACCESS.md` decisions | They become Loop 8 defects instead of Loop 1 shapes. The ones that matter cannot be fixed by then — you redraw |
390	| §4's derivation, picking from the family list instead | The training-data reflex, which is the exact thing the derivation exists to route around |
391	| §7's second and third concept | The choice. One concept is a proposal presented as a conclusion |
392	| The two distinctness tests | The word "distinct" doing all the work, which is what six of seven audited skills already ship |
393	| §8's per-class ratio | Three quarters of the model's fidelity spent on background, on every mobile surface |
394	| §10's set check | Nine images with the same composition, which reads as one idea rendered nine times |
395	| Gate A | The direction choice. You pick; they see it at Gate B, with prototypes already built against it |

# Loop 1 — Direction

**Goal:** decide what this surface is, who it is for, what it must not become, and what it
looks like — and get a human to agree before anything expensive exists.

**Input:** [`TRANSLATE.md`](../TRANSLATE.md), all six rows filled. Row 1 blank means this
loop cannot start; it does not start generic.

**Output:** the direction half of `DIRECTION.md`, one rendered image per surface per
concept, and a signed Gate A.

```text
0 branch        1 class        2 platform      3 access        4 derive
redesign or     page-shaped    iOS / Android   the Loop 1      physical experience
greenfield      tool-shaped    or neutral      decision list   → three directions
                                                                     │
5 palette ─► 6 type ─► 7 concepts ─► 8 ratio ─► 9 dispatch ─► 10 set check ─► Gate A
per          per        one per       per class  one agent per  per concept,    human
direction,   direction  direction,    announce   surface per    anti-repeat     decides
sampled once            both tests    N first    concept
```

---

## The fork

Read row 1 of `TRANSLATE.md` before anything else in this file, because it changes what
every step below is looking for.

**Page-shaped** — read for seconds, once. The concepts compete on the opening move: what a
viewer understands in three seconds without reading a word. The surface list is a scroll
order. The images are horizontal, the aspect ratios in §8 below say which.

**Tool-shaped** — read for hours, daily, by the same person. The concepts compete on the
operator's day: which of the forty-times-a-day actions gets the layout. The surface list is
a screen inventory keyed to tasks, not a scroll. `§15` binds **[HARD]** here, which means
the keyboard map is a Loop 1 artifact and not a Loop 4 discovery, and `STYLES.md`'s
style-under-density line is a gating question rather than a note.

Both classes run every step below. They answer them differently, and the places where the
answer forks are marked.

---

## 0. Branch: is this a redesign?

A surface that already exists is not a blank page, and running this loop as if it were is
how a working position gets replaced by a template with better spacing.

Read [`REDESIGN.md`](../REDESIGN.md) and classify the ask before anything else. It is a
fork, not a slider — there is no "mostly a correction."

| Classification | What this loop does |
|---|---|
| **Greenfield** | Start at §1 below. Nothing to preserve, so nothing to ask |
| **Correction** — the position is right, execution drifted | **This loop does not run.** `REDESIGN.md`'s fix ladder runs against the extracted system, with its per-fix discipline as the stop. Any fix that touches position leaves the pass and escalates to Gate A |
| **Reposition** — the position itself is wrong | This loop runs **in full**, with `CURRENT.md` as an input constraint rather than a blank page, and with the survival list written *before* §1 below rather than during it |
| **Conformance** — `TRANSLATE.md` row 6 names a design system the surface must obey | Neither path. `TRANSLATE.md`'s escape hatch fires, `PRINCIPLES.md`'s `§1`–`§3` are suspended wholesale
(that file's rules, not this file's steps), and `BREAKING.md`'s recording rule covers writing that down. Route to conformance and say so plainly |

**On the reposition path, two things enter this loop that a greenfield run never carries.**
`CURRENT.md` — the extracted rendered system, measured and not yet adjudicated — is an input
to §4 below, because a derived direction that ignores what is already on the screen is a
greenfield direction wearing a redesign's name. And the **survival list**: what is
load-bearing, in `REDESIGN.md`'s sense of what breaks *outside* this surface if it changes.
Every concept in §7 below is built against that list, and a concept that quietly drops an
item on it has not been proposed, it has been mis-scoped.

**The classification is falsifiable and the gates check it.** Three Gate A rejections on a
correction path means the ask was a reposition all along. The escalation runs one way only.

---

## 1. Set the surface class

`TRANSLATE.md` row 1: `page-shaped` or `tool-shaped`, set once **per surface**, not once per
product. A product with a marketing site and an application behind login is two runs sharing
a palette and a type system, not one run averaging them — and the averaged run is the one
that ships a dashboard with a landing page's spacing scale.

Write it in `DIRECTION.md` now. Every file this loop reads forks on it first.

## 2. Set platform mode, if this runs on a phone or a tablet

[`SURFACES.md`](../SURFACES.md) §1 — **iOS-native**, **Android-native**, or
**cross-platform-neutral**. One branch, chosen before a style and before a target number,
written into `DIRECTION.md` before Gate A.

They do not mix. A neutral surface that borrows Liquid Glass for its content cards has
broken Apple's rule and its own in one move. A platform-committed surface that adopts the
other platform's numbers is wrong on both. `SURFACES.md` carries every number; none of them
are opinions and none of them get rounded.

Web-only, desktop-only surfaces skip this step and record that they skipped it.

## 3. Run the `ACCESS.md` Loop 1 decisions

[`ACCESS.md`](../ACCESS.md) §13 is a list of thirteen decisions both classes owe, six more
tool-shaped, and four more native. **They run here, before a single image generates**, and
they land in `DIRECTION.md` as answers.

This is not an audit moved earlier. These are shapes, not defects: a non-drag affordance
occupies layout space, a grid and a table are two different keyboard experiences of the same
visual, a focus ring has to be drawn against every background it can land on. None of them
are fixable in Loop 8 — you redraw.

Three of them constrain the next two steps directly and are worth doing in order: whether
the sampled accent can carry body text, a 3:1 graphical role, or neither (which constrains
§5 below); the contrast boundary, stated rather than assumed; and the target-size route,
whose spacing unit enters the scale before the type scale does.

`§10` is **[HARD]**. A row the human chooses not to answer is recorded as a decision with
its cost per `§16`, never as silence.

## 4. Derive the direction — do not pick one

Invoke [`STYLES.md`](../STYLES.md)'s **"Before the list: derive, don't pick"** procedure,
then its five-input **"Picking one"** procedure. In that order. The first generates, the
second cuts, and running them backwards produces a shortlist that started in a catalog.

The short version, because the failure it prevents is the most common one in this pipeline:
read the archetype words from `TRANSLATE.md` row 4, ask what physical, spatial, or material
experience would embody them if design were not involved, and derive three visual directions
from *that*. Each stated in one concrete sentence naming a real-world referent. **If your
sentence contains only adjectives, it is not concrete enough**, and if you find yourself
reaching for a Swiss grid or a terminal by reflex you are reading your training data rather
than the subject.

Then read the families — to name what you derived, to learn what it implies technically, and
to be warned how it fails. Not to generate it.

**What this step hands to the next one, stated because the singular is a trap.**
`STYLES.md` ends its procedure with *"never one answer — bring three directions to Gate A."*
That is binding, and it means **the directions do not collapse here.** Two or three survive

concepts are the same objects at two stages of development, not two rounds of generation.

So §5 and §6 below run **once per surviving direction**, not once for the run — a letterpress
direction and a cockpit direction do not share a neutral ramp or a typeface, and a palette
built before the directions exist is a palette built for none of them. The one thing genuinely
shared is the sampled accent, because the subject has one logo (§5 below).

Two further outputs of this step are gating and both are easy to skip:

- **The collision or subversion**, per `STYLES.md`, per direction. One parent carries
  structure, the other carries surface, and which is which gets named now rather than during
  the build.
- **The style-under-density line**, in the form *at forty rows this does X*. Asked at Gate A
  because the answer is sometimes *it cannot* — and a direction that is beautiful, coherent,
  correct for the archetype and structurally incapable of the surface it was chosen for is a
  finding worth having before the images are signed off. Tool-shaped surfaces cannot proceed
  without this line. Page-shaped surfaces owe it wherever real data lands.

## 5. Palette — sampled from reality, in OKLCH, as pairs

**Sampled once. Built out per direction.** `§6`: pull the accent from the subject or product's
real logo, product, or work. Sample the pixels. There is one subject and one logo, so there is
one sample, and every direction from §4 above reconciles against it. No existing brand means a
deliberate choice defended by one sentence of physical scene, then reconciled against
`TRANSLATE.md` row 3.

Then build out **once per direction**: an accent, a substrate, a neutral ramp, and the full
state set — and tool-shaped, the status vocabulary from `TOOLS.md`, which needs shape or label
as well as color because `§10` forbids color alone. The same sampled hex sits at a different
chroma, against a different substrate, in a different ramp in each of the two or three
directions; that divergence is a large part of what Gate A is choosing between.

Work in **OKLCH**, and write gradient endpoints in `oklch()`, because a single hex or `rgb()`
endpoint silently drops the whole interpolation back to muddy sRGB.

**Every color ships as a pair** — the swatch and the foreground that is legal on it, with its
measured ratio at the size it is actually used (`STYLES.md`, paired color tokens). A swatch
with no foreground is an unfinished token and does not enter `DIRECTION.md`. Pairs extend to
every state and to the focus ring, and they are paired **per mode**: a foreground legal on
the light swatch tells you nothing about the dark one.

Declare now whether the two modes are one design in two palettes or **two art directions**.
If the derived direction is atmospheric, motion-native, or material-heavy, the answer is two
art directions and both get built.

## 6. Type

**Per direction, like §5 above.** Two families at most, one if the direction earns it. Variable where the design drives an
axis, self-hosted and subset per `§7`, and checked against the actual script per `§13` — a
Persian, Arabic, or Devanagari subject needs a face that draws it, not one that falls back.

**Every font decision carries its reason on the same line**: what this face does for this
direction that the obvious one would not. `STYLES.md`'s ban is on convergence, not on the
typeface — a bare blacklist goes stale in eighteen months and a reason survives.

Tool-shaped surfaces add one requirement here: tabular figures on every column of numbers
that updates. It is one declaration and it is not optional.

## 7. Develop each direction into a concept

One concept per surviving direction from §4 above, carrying that direction's palette and type
from §5 and §6. This is development, not a fresh generation — a concept invented here, with no
direction behind it, has skipped the derivation and will read like it.

The conductor does this, not a worker. `§1`–`§4` are asking for the collision, the opening
move, and the thing nobody expects, and that is exactly where a cheaper model reaches for
the category reflex these rules exist to prevent.

Each concept states:

- **The collision or subversion**, as one sentence, with the structural parent named
- **The opening move** — page-shaped, what happens in the first three seconds; tool-shaped,
  what the operator sees when they open this at 9am with forty things waiting
- **How the primary content is presented** — invent it. Not a card grid by reflex: a flexible
  card layout puts each item's attributes in a different place from the last, so a reader
  comparing them scans back and forth hunting for what moved. A list, a table, or a filmstrip
  holds position from item to item and is the more honest default whenever the things
  genuinely are comparable
- **How navigation works**, and tool-shaped, the keyboard path through the primary workflow
- **What happens when something is missing or wrong** — page-shaped, the 404 and the failed
  submission, in this concept rather than the framework's default. Tool-shaped, `TOOLS.md`'s
  nine data states, with empty, permission denied, and conflict named specifically: the first
  is what every new user sees, the last is the one that destroys work
- **The surface list and its order**, derived from row 2's viewer and their task

### The two distinctness tests

`§4` says bring 2–3 distinct concepts. As a bare instruction that is what six of seven
audited skills already fail at, two of them by asking the model to simulate a random number
generator — which returns its prior with extra steps. So distinctness is tested **on the
artifact**, not asserted about the process. Both tests run before anything reaches Gate A.

> **Swap test.** If someone could swap the headline text between two concepts without
> noticing, they are too similar.
>
> **Tool-shaped surfaces frequently have no headline**, so swap what they do have: the screen
> title, the primary action's label, and the empty state's copy. If all three move between two
> concepts unnoticed, the concepts differ in styling and not in how the operator's day is
> organized — which is the only axis this class is choosing on.

> **Family pass.** Label each concept with a concrete noun of your own choosing — *exhibition,
> cockpit, playbill, field-manual*. If two share a label, or a label applies equally well to
> another concept, rework. Do not use a fixed vocabulary for the labels; a fixed vocabulary is
> the catalog problem again, one level up.

Then the **category-reflex check**, from `STYLES.md`'s cliché fence: if a concept is guessable
from "surface for a \<category\>" alone, or from category-plus-obvious-twist, throw it out.
Note one concept you rejected and why, so the human sees the range rather than the survivors.

## 8. Aspect ratio, keyed to the surface class

**This is where a real bug lived.** "One horizontal image per surface" was inherited from a
parent whose surfaces were all web page sections. A phone screen is roughly 9:19.5; rendering
it on a 16:9 canvas spends about three quarters of the model's fidelity budget on empty
background. State the ratio per class:

| Surface | Canvas | What is in it |
|---|---|---|
| Page-shaped web section | 16:9, hero 21:9 | One section |
| Tool-shaped desktop screen | 16:10 | One screen, full chrome, real row counts |
| Phone screen | 4:5 for one screen, or 16:9 holding 2–3 phone-portrait screens at identical scale | One step of the flow |
| Tablet screen | 4:3 or 16:10 | One screen, at a stated width |

Two to three phones on one canvas is the **only** exception to never compressing a board,
and it holds because they are the same surface across a flow at readable scale rather than
different surfaces stacked. The moment type stops being legible, drop to one phone per canvas.

**Announce N before generating.** **N is the surface count, not the image count** — and every
concept is rendered across all N, so three concepts and nine surfaces is twenty-seven images.
Write both numbers in text before generating — *"three concepts, nine surfaces, twenty-seven
images"* — and label every image **"\<concept label>: Surface X of N — \<name\>"**, with the
label from the family pass in §7 above, so the three renders of the same surface never collide.

That 3× is the real cost of `§4` and it is paid deliberately. **If it is not affordable, cut to
two concepts rather than to a partial set** — a concept rendered at three surfaces cannot be
compared against one rendered at nine, and the set-level check in §10 below has nothing to run
on. Two complete concepts is a choice. Three partial ones is a preference dressed as one.

Committing to the numbers first makes stopping early a visible contradiction rather than a
silent one, and silent under-generation is the failure this costs one line to prevent.

## 9. Dispatch `surface-designer`

**One agent per surface per concept, one image each.** Never compress multiple surfaces into
one board, and never compress two concepts into one either: a
compressed board hides exactly the detail the human needs to judge, and what it hides first is
the smallest type and the primary action.

Each agent receives the concept, the palette with its pairs, the type system, the collision
sentence, the platform mode, and the aspect ratio for its class. Each returns its image, its
logged composition anchor, and its logged background mode — the log exists so §10 below has
something to compare, since no single worker can see its neighbors.

A second **detail image** of the same surface is permitted on demand, focused on typography
and spacing at larger scale, when the human at Gate A cannot read something. It is not a
redesign and not a variant: same design system, cleaner render.

## 10. The set-level check

Run by the conductor, on what comes back, **once per concept** — the set is one concept's N
surfaces, since that is the set a human reads as one thing. No worker can run it.

Reject the set and regenerate the offending surfaces if:

- the same **composition anchor** repeats more than **twice in a row**
- the same **background mode** repeats more than **three times in a row**
- **no full-bleed treatment appears anywhere** in the set

**Suspended for a deliberately minimal brief** — typography-only, ultra-reductive, restraint
as the stated direction. There, sameness is the design and this check would be arguing with
the brief. Say out loud that it was suspended and why, so a later reader does not read a
uniform set as an oversight.

Also check what the set does *not* vary: **within one concept**, palette, type hierarchy,
component family, and surface treatment stay identical across every image. Composition,
emphasis, and visual tempo are where variation belongs. A set that varies the palette has not
produced range, it has produced three different products. Across concepts the opposite holds —
palette and type *must* differ, because that is what §5 and §6 above built per direction and
what Gate A is choosing between.

---

> ## Gate A — human decision. `§16` **[HARD]**
>
> **Presented:**
>
> - **The rendered images**, per concept, all N surfaces of each, labeled
> - **The palette per concept**, as pairs, each with its measured ratio, and the one sampled
>   source they all reconcile against
> - **The type system per concept**, each family with its reason on the same line
> - **The collision sentence** per concept, with the structural parent named
> - **The style-under-density line** — *at forty rows this does X*
> - **The `ACCESS.md` answers**, and any row deferred, with its cost
> - **A SAFE / RISK split**, below. Not optional and not one risk
>
> **The SAFE / RISK split.** Coherence is table stakes; this is the part that separates one
> run from another. Present the safe reading of the direction, then **at least two risks**,
> each with **what it costs** if it lands badly — in bytes, in build time, in the audience it
> loses, in the thing it makes harder later. A risk with no stated cost is a pitch. Two risks
> is the floor because one risk is a recommendation wearing a choice's clothes.
>
> **The anti-shortcut clause.** This gate is not a status update and `DIRECTION.md` is not a
> substitute for it: **the written output is the OUTPUT of the interactive review**. If there
> is any non-trivial finding, the path to proceeding goes through the human. A gate that
> becomes a paragraph somebody reads later has been removed, not satisfied.
>
> **They may pick a concept, pick pieces across concepts, or send it back.** Iterating here
> is far cheaper than iterating in code, and this is the last point where the direction is
> free to move.
>
> **Deferrals get priced, in a table:**
>
> | decision needed | if deferred, what happens |
> |---|---|
> | Reduced-motion still frame not art-directed | Ships as `animation: none` — a plain freeze where a composed frame was |
> | Second and third concept not generated | The direction has nothing to be chosen against; the first idea wins by default, which is `§1`'s failure mode |
> | Style-under-density line not written | A family that cannot hold forty rows is discovered at build, with the images already approved |
> | `ACCESS.md` grid-or-table row left open | The keyboard model gets decided by whoever writes the component, in Loop 4, from the visual |
> | Platform mode left unset on a native surface | Every number below it forks, and discovering the fork during the build is a rewrite |
>
> State the cost once, accept the answer, carry it into the run's confidence, and do not
> raise it again.

---

## When Gate A rejects

**Diagnose before regenerating anything.** The three rejections go to three different places
and treating them alike is how a run burns its budget re-rendering a correct image.

| What was rejected | Where it goes back to |
|---|---|
| **Execution** — wrong palette in the render, wrong crop, the image did not capture the concept | Regenerate those images with corrected direction. Same concept, same surface list, same collision |
| **Concept** — the collision does not land, the opening move is wrong, the content is presented wrong | Back to §7 above. New concepts, not a patch on the rejected one |
| **Brief** — their reaction reveals the surface class, the viewer, the archetype, or the anti-positioning was misread | Back to `TRANSLATE.md`. Fix the table first. Designing on a misread table produces another rejection at the same gate |

The third row is the one that gets missed. **When the human says the images look fine and
still sounds unhappy, the table is the suspect, not the render.**

**Three rejections at the same gate means the translation table is wrong, not the work.**
Stop iterating. Re-open `TRANSLATE.md`, fix the row that is wrong, and come back through this
gate. The fourth attempt at the same gate has never worked. On a redesign, that same count
carries the second diagnosis from §0 above: three Gate A rejections on a correction path
means the ask was a reposition from the start.

**Record what the rejection revealed**, not only the correction. What they reacted against,
and what that says about the viewer, the archetype, or the risk appetite the table failed to
capture. Recording only the correction throws away the more valuable half of it.

## Skip costs

| Skipping | Costs |
|---|---|
| §3, the `ACCESS.md` decisions | They become Loop 8 defects instead of Loop 1 shapes. The ones that matter cannot be fixed by then — you redraw |
| §4's derivation, picking from the family list instead | The training-data reflex, which is the exact thing the derivation exists to route around |
| §7's second and third concept | The choice. One concept is a proposal presented as a conclusion |
| The two distinctness tests | The word "distinct" doing all the work, which is what six of seven audited skills already ship |
| §8's per-class ratio | Three quarters of the model's fidelity spent on background, on every mobile surface |
| §10's set check | Nine images with the same composition, which reads as one idea rendered nine times |
| Gate A | The direction choice. You pick; they see it at Gate B, with prototypes already built against it |

22	## The fork
23	
24	**Page-shaped** — read for seconds, once. A technique is evidence of capability and a carrier
25	of argument: three seconds to make a viewer understand something a paragraph would have taken
26	thirty seconds to say. The budget is a first-paint budget and the audience arrives cold on an
27	unknown device. This class owes `CRAFT.md`'s **three render states**.
28	
29	**Tool-shaped** — read for hours, daily, by the same person. A technique is something the
30	operator pays for every day, and a scroll-linked reveal that delights once is a tax on the
31	four-hundredth repetition. The arsenal inverts: the heavy groups mostly cost and the
32	unglamorous ones mostly pay — grid determinism, information design, icon discipline, a
33	hairline that does not double. This class owes `TOOLS.md`'s **nine data states**, and `§15`
34	binds **[HARD]**.
35	
36	A tool-shaped surface carrying heavy motion owes **both sets**. They are different axes, not
37	a longer list: render states answer *can this machine and this person's settings display it*,
38	data states answer *what is true of the data right now*. Cross them; do not concatenate them.
39	
40	---
41	
42	## 1. Assign a technique per surface
43	
44	For each surface, assign a technique from [`CRAFT.md`](../CRAFT.md) that serves the style
45	already approved at Gate A. Style decides what is on the table; the technique executes it.
46	Reaching for a style because you want to use a shader is the tail wagging the dog and it
47	shows in the output.
48	
49	**Every assignment passes `CRAFT.md`'s three-question test**, three answers, one line each:
50	
51	1. What does this make the viewer **understand** about the subject or the product? *"It looks
52	   impressive"* — cut it.
53	2. Which **objection** does it answer, or which **proof** does it carry? None — demote it to a
54	   decorative layer with a stated byte budget.
55	3. What does it cost in **bytes and main-thread time**? Unknown — prototype it before it
56	   enters the design.
57	
58	Tool-shaped reads question two as *which part of the operator's day does this make shorter*
59	and question three as *what does it cost on the four-hundredth repetition*.
60	
61	A technique answering all three is worth building at any complexity. One answering none is
62	worth nothing at any complexity, and no gate grants an exemption.
63	
64	**Spend the budget where the surface is decided.** Page-shaped: the opening, the moment the
65	product is shown, and the moment just before the ask. Tool-shaped: the two or three objects
66	the operator touches forty times a day, with the other thirty left quiet. Expression
67	everywhere is the same failure as restraint everywhere — a flat field with more noise in it.
68	
69	## 2. Dispatch `technique-prototyper`
70	
71	**One agent per technique.** Each researches it properly, builds a standalone runnable HTML
72	proof, screenshots it, measures frame rate under load, records the byte cost, and builds every
73	state the surface class owes. Free rein while prototyping — any library, any CDN, any
74	reference — and that freedom ends at handoff, where `§7` requires everything vendored.
75	
76	**Report failure honestly. Failing cheap here is the entire point of the loop.** A technique
77	that fails prototyping does not reach Gate B: it is not proposed, not promised, and not built
78	anyway on the theory that it comes together in integration. Failing here costs one file and
79	twenty minutes. Failing in the build costs the surface, the layout designed around it, and
80	the copy written to fit.

82	### Verdicts carry an evidence label
83	
84	Every verdict is **ship**, **cut**, or **ship-with-caveat**, and every verdict carries one of
85	three labels. **Never guess. State the source.**
86	
87	| Label | What it means | What it looks like written down |
88	|---|---|---|
89	| **TESTED** | Measured, on a named machine, at a named viewport, with the number recorded | *"58fps sustained, 1440×900, M2 Air, 6× CPU throttle, 12k instances"* |

91	| **INFERRED** | Not measured. From the library's documentation, a reference implementation, or reasoning | *"the library documents 60fps at 10k instances; not run here"* |
92	
93	A frame rate measured on one machine at one viewport is not the same claim as one inferred,
94	and collapsing them is how a number that was always a guess arrives at the build wearing a
95	measurement's authority. **A `ship` verdict on an INFERRED frame rate is a proposal, not a
96	proof** — it goes to Gate B labeled as one, and the human decides whether to buy it.

100	Undocumented motion gets rebuilt three times, differently each time. Motion character comes

107	- **Easing as a named curve with its coefficients** — `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, named

109	- **Stagger in ms, with a cap**, so a list of forty rows does not take eight seconds to

111	- **Exit shorter than enter.** A departure that takes as long as an arrival reads as lag.
112	- **What triggers what**, and the scroll mapping if there is one. `IntersectionObserver`,

118	  techniques, and two of them — replacing z-axis transitions with fades, and not animating

226	  **Community Group Draft of 30 July 2026**. It is **not** a W3C Recommendation and calling it
227	  "the W3C design token standard" is wrong in the same checkable way as any other fabricated
228	  citation. Pin the draft by date: the value shapes have already changed between drafts.
229	- **`dimension` is an object, not a string.** `{ "value": 16, "unit": "px" }` — and the unit

271	    },

304	> - **Every verdict with its evidence label** — TESTED, PARTIAL, or INFERRED — and the machine

325	> | `tokens.json` not written | The build step reads values out of prose, and the first transcription error is silent |
326	> | Tier-2 budget left undeclared | The heavy layer sizes itself, and the number is discovered on a mid-range Android after launch |

336	prototype is never argued into acceptance, tuned during the build, or carried forward on the

338	test the original faced.
